hook
An electric car has no engine, no gears to shift, no exhaust pipe. Yet it's quicker off the line than many sports cars. How?
xray
Let's look inside. Under the floor sits a giant battery, and at the wheels, an electric motor.
battery
The battery is made of thousands of small cells, like the ones in your phone, all packed together.
battery
Press the pedal, and electricity flows from the battery to an inverter, which turns it into the right kind of power for the motor.
motor
Inside the motor, coils of wire become electromagnets. They switch on and off in a spinning pattern, pulling a magnet rotor round and round.
motor
The spinning rotor turns the wheels. No explosions, no pistons. That's why electric cars are so quiet and smooth.
torque
And an electric motor gives full pushing power instantly, right from zero speed. That's why it shoots off the line!
regen
Here's the coolest trick. When you slow down, the motor flips roles and becomes a generator.
regen
The car's motion spins it, making electricity that flows back into the battery. This is called regenerative braking.
eff
Electric motors turn about ninety percent of their energy into motion. A petrol engine wastes most of its energy as heat.
charge
Then just plug it in, and the battery fills back up, ready for the next drive.
outro
Battery, motor, wheels. Simple, smart, and silent. Follow for more science made simple!
